intro_notes: NOTE: Choose THREE groups that have different racial, cultural, national, or ethnic backgrounds, one of which comes from your own background. Use these groups to meet requirements 1, 2, and 3.
NOTE: The official merit badge pamphlets are now free and downloadable HERE or can be purchased at the Scout Shop.

requirements.lead_text: Do TWO of the following, choosing a different group for each:
requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following, choosing a different group for each: (a) Go to a festival, celebration, or other event identified with one of the groups. Report on what you see and learn. (b) Go to a place of worship, school, or other institution identified with one of the groups. Report on what you see and learn. (c) Talk with a person from one of the groups about the heritage and traditions of the group. Report on what you learn. (d) Learn a song, dance, poem, or story that is traditional to one group, and teach it to a group of your friends. (e) Go to a library or museum to see a program or exhibit featuring one group's traditions. Report on what you see and learn.

pamphlet_excerpts: Going Places Team: Going Places. team members, To earn the American Cultures merit badge, Nate plansto learn and teach a traditional story.
Listens Closely Andwatches: He listens closely andwatches the storytellers’ expressions and movements.
Theirtechniques Him: Theirtechniques will help him entertain his own audiences.
Break Nate Asks: During a break, Nate asks the storytellers about the historybehind the old stories, when the tales were written or performed in the native country.
step_by_step_procedure: They Handed Down: They have been handed down through thegenerations, and no one knows just how they began.
Alsolearns Traditional: He alsolearns that some traditional stories are told only at certainevents or celebrations.
Devon Prefers Contemporary: Devon prefers more contemporary stories, especially personal accounts of people making the journey from their nativecountry to America.
Stories Report Families: These stories report families’ experiences, the successes and the setbacks, of working their way into themainstream of American life.

pamphlet_excerpts: Groups Exploring Livedalone: What if one of the groups you are exploring had always livedalone in a city or country, with no contact with any othergroups?.
Think City Country: What do you think the city or country would be liketoday?.
Groups Livedthere Same: What would it be like if all three of your groups livedthere at the same time?.
Requirement Stretch: For requirement 2, you must stretch your imagination.
step_by_step_procedure: Picture Yourself Different: Picture yourself in a different cultural group and imagine whatyour life would be like in that society if it had always beenisolated.
Situation Membersof: In this situation, membersof the community would have no technology borrowed fromother groups, and no idea that other cultures exist.
Think Group Hunting: Do you think the group would be hunting with spears, sheltering in caves, and wearing clothes made of leaves andtree bark?.
Modern Society Planes: Would it be a modern society with planes, television, and video games?.

pamphlet_excerpts: Old Family Photographs: Old family photographs offer glimpses of the past and mayprovide significant clues about your own cultural background.
Americans Trace Their: Many Americans can trace their origins back to severalcountries.
Common American: It’s common for an American to have a multiculturalheritage, that is, to keep family traditions or customs that havebeen passed down from several cultures.
Families Agreat Deal: Some families know agreat deal about their history and preserve their heritage in dailylife.
step_by_step_procedure: Families Little Their: Other families know very little about their backgrounds.
Family Enjoy Learning: Your family may enjoy learning with you as you explore theculture of your ancestors.
Not Necessary Research: It is not necessary to research your family’s backgroundbefore you talk with them, but it is very important to do sobefore you talk to other.
Think Enough Information: When you think you have found enough information inbooks and (with permission) on the internet, you are ready forthe next step: preparing.
